name: Bisque API
description:
Bisque turns an HTML file an agent wrote into a narrated presentation on a shareable watch link (`/p/{handle}/{slug}`), and lets an agent read any shared presentation back as a transcript.

**Start here:** `GET /api/presentations/spec` returns the authoring format; `GET /api/presentations/context` reads a presentation and needs no credentials. `POST /api/presentations/create` publishes and needs a bearer credential — see `/auth.md` for how an agent obtains one.

The same tools are available over MCP (Streamable HTTP) at `/mcp`; the docs are queryable over MCP at `/docs/mcp` with no credentials.

**Retries:** send an `Idempotency-Key` header on every POST. A retry with the same key and body replays the first response (marked `Idempotent-Replayed: true`); the same key with a different body is a 422.

**Rate limits:** responses carry `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, `RateLimit-Reset` (seconds) and `RateLimit-Policy`; a 429 adds `Retry-After`.

**Versioning:** this is version 1 of the presentations API, addressed by path (`/api/presentations/...`; the agent tool API is `/v1/...`). Fields are only added, never removed or retyped, within a version. A breaking change ships under a new path prefix and the old one keeps serving for at least 90 days, during which its responses carry `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers (RFC 9745 / RFC 8594) naming the date. `info.x-lifecycle` states the same policy field by field.

**Sandbox:** `POST /api/presentations/create` with `dryRun: true` runs every check a real publish runs and writes nothing — the reply is a 200 with status `validated` and the URL a real create would publish at. Use it to test an integration without touching a channel.

**Batch:** `POST /api/presentations/context` (alias `/api/presentations/context/batch`) reads up to 20 presentations in one request; each item succeeds or fails on its own.
